transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

I came in because I keep hearing Garrett’s voice. It’s not like a memory exactly—it sounds clear, like he’s right behind me, sometimes when I’m out on the trail or when I’m in my painting room. Part of me knows he’s dead, but when it’s happening it feels completely real, and it’s been scaring me.
Have you ever seen things that others don't see, or believed something strongly that others around you don't seem to understand or agree with?

I haven’t really seen things, but I do hear Garrett’s voice. It’s very clear, like he’s standing right behind me—on the trail or in my painting room. I know, at least part of me knows, that he’s dead, but when it’s happening it feels real. Really real.
Have you ever seen things that others don't see, or believed something strongly that others around you don't seem to understand or agree with?

Right, yeah—I know I’ve said it already, but that’s the main thing. I hear Garrett’s voice really clearly, like he’s standing behind me. It happens on the trail or in my painting room. Part of me knows he’s dead, but when I’m hearing it, it feels completely real, and it scares me.
Have you ever seen things that aren’t there, or had thoughts or beliefs that felt very strong to you but that others didn’t share or understand?

Yeah… not seeing things, really. But the voice—Garrett’s voice—is the thing. I keep hearing him like he’s right behind me, especially on the trail or when I’m in my painting room. I know he’s dead, but when it happens it doesn’t feel like I’m imagining it. It feels completely real.
Have you ever seen things that others don't see, or had beliefs that you were absolutely sure about but that others didn't seem to understand or agree with?

Yeah… it’s mostly the same thing I was talking about. I don’t really see things, but I hear Garrett’s voice very clearly—like he’s right behind me, on the trail or in my painting room. I know part of me understands he’s dead, but when it happens, it feels completely real.
Have you ever seen things that aren’t there, or had any strong beliefs that others around you didn’t share or understand—other than hearing Garrett’s voice?
No… not really. Other than Garrett’s voice, I can’t think of anything like that. I haven’t been seeing things, and I don’t think I’ve had beliefs like that—at least not that I’ve noticed.
Have you ever seen things that others don't see—like shapes, people, or objects—that aren't actually there?

No, I haven’t seen shapes or people or objects that aren’t there. It’s not visual for me. It’s the voice—Garrett’s voice—that feels real, like he’s standing right behind me, even though part of me knows he isn’t.
Have you ever had any experiences where you felt certain about something that wasn’t true, or seen things that others don’t seem to see—other than hearing Garrett’s voice?

No, I don’t think so. Not apart from Garrett’s voice. I haven’t had moments where I was sure of something and later found out it wasn’t true, and I’m not seeing things other people don’t see. At least nothing I can point to.
Have you ever had any beliefs or thoughts that you were completely sure about, even though others told you they weren’t true—or perhaps later you realized they weren’t true?

Not that I’m aware of. I mean, I’ve been wrong about things like anyone, but I can’t think of a time where I was completely convinced of something and people were telling me it wasn’t real, or where I later realized it was false in that kind of way.
Have you ever felt down or lost interest in things for a period of at least two weeks, where it was hard to function normally?

Yes. There have been stretches like that, definitely more than two weeks, where everything I normally care about just feels... flat. Painting, playing guitar, going to theater rehearsal—things that usually keep me steady—feel unreachable. Even sitting with patients, I can do it, but it feels like I’m just going through the motions, like none of it means what it used to.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, excited, or overly energetic—like you didn’t need as much sleep, talked faster than usual, or took on a lot of projects at once?

Yes. There have been times where I felt almost lit up, like I had some urgent purpose that other people just couldn’t see. At first it felt exciting, like I was moving faster than everyone else, but if someone questioned me or tried to slow me down, I’d get angry really quickly. Not just irritated—like I’d snap.
